---
title: Save a list as a view
description: Save a query, a sort and a grouping as a view, so every app lists the same items the same way, then change, delete or read it.
---

A [view](/catalog/view) saves a listing so every app shows the same one. Its `query` says which items it lists, and its `sort` and `group` say in what order and how they group. **How an app draws the items is the app's own**, so a view holds no layout. In the TypeScript example, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows.

## Create a view

[Create a view](/reference/api/views/createView) with a `title`, and the settings you need. This one lists tasks, soonest due first and then by title, grouped by priority:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa views create --title "Tasks by priority" \
  --query '{"types":["core.task"]}' \
  --sort '[{"by":"properties.due_at","direction":"asc"},{"by":"title","direction":"asc"}]' \
  --group '{"by":"properties.priority"}'
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /views
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "title": "Tasks by priority",
  "query": { "types": ["core.task"] },
  "sort": [
    { "by": "properties.due_at", "direction": "asc" },
    { "by": "title", "direction": "asc" }
  ],
  "group": { "by": "properties.priority" }
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.POST("/views", {
  body: {
    title: "Tasks by priority",
    query: { types: ["core.task"] },
    sort: [
      { by: "properties.due_at", direction: "asc" },
      { by: "title", direction: "asc" },
    ],
    group: { by: "properties.priority" },
  },
});
```

The answer is the view as a `system.view` item at `version` 1, with its settings as its properties. It holds no items: [read the view](/build/read-a-view) for those.

## The settings

- **`title`**, which is required: up to 500 characters.
- **`query`**, which items the view lists:
  - `types`: up to 100 types, each with the types beneath it.
  - `state`: `active`, `archived` or both. Active and archived when absent.
  - `tier`: `library`, `feed` or `all`. Both when absent.
  - `filter`: any expression that [List, filter and search](/build/list-filter-search#filter-by-properties) describes. A view of one collection's members is `edge[in-collection] eq "<collection id>"`, and of one writer's items, `source eq "<source>"`.
  - `beneath`: an item, to list it and everything under it by `parent-of`.
- **`sort`**, up to 10 keys of `by` and `direction`, applied in turn. `by` is an item's own field (`title`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `occurred_at`, `type`, `state`, `tier` or `tags`), `last_activity_at`, or `properties.<name>`. A view with no sort lists the newest `occurred_at` first.
- **`group`**, with a `by` from the same fields, or `edge[<type>]` or `backref[<type>]` to group by what items link to. Add a `bucket` of `day`, `week`, `month` or `year` to group a date field by period, `order` to put chosen groups first, and `hidden` to leave groups out of the groups an app reads while still listing their items. The server lists a view's items without grouping them; a [working copy](/build/read-a-view#read-a-view-from-a-working-copy) groups them.

A view never lists `system.*` items, and never widens what a credential reads: each app sees only the items its own credential reaches.

## Change a view

[Update a view](/reference/api/views/updateView) with the `version` you read and the settings you change. Each setting you name is replaced whole. To stop grouping, send `group` as `null`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa views update <view-id> --version 1 --group null
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /views/<view-id>
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 1, "group": null }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.PATCH("/views/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id: viewId } },
  body: { version: 1, group: null },
});
```

The answer holds the view at its next version. A change sent with an older version still applies when nobody has changed the same setting since. When someone has, Marfa answers `409 version_conflict`, with `conflicting_fields` naming each setting and `current` holding the view as it is now. Read it, decide, and send the change again with the new version.

## Delete or read a view

- **To delete a view,** [delete it](/reference/api/views/deleteView) or run `marfa views delete`. It's gone at once, with no bin.
- **To read a view's settings,** run `marfa views get`, [get it](/reference/api/items/getItem) as an item, or list the type `system.view`.
- **To read the items it lists,** run `marfa views items`, as [Read a view](/build/read-a-view) shows.

When the item a view sits under by `parent-of` is deleted, the view is revoked: it can still be read and deleted, but refuses a change or a read of its items with `400 invalid_transition`.

## When a write is refused

Marfa checks every setting before it writes anything:

- `400 validation_error` for a malformed setting, named in `details.errors[0].path`, such as `group.bucket` for a bucket on `title`. A key the settings don't declare is named in `details.unknown_body_fields`.
- `400 unknown_type` for a type in `query.types` that nothing registers.
- `400 missing_required_field` for a create with no `title`, or a change with no `version`.
- `403 type_not_permitted` when the credential can't write `system.view`. Writing a view needs write on `system.view`, and reading one needs read. `content:read` and `content:write` reach no `system.*` type.
- `404 item_not_found` for an ID that holds no view the credential can read.

The rules are in the [views](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/views.md) chapter of the contract.
